entries.value: For a Strategic Value claim, a counterfactual comparison must identify the same decision-relevant initial conditions, utility measure, exogenous context and time basis across intervention and baseline worlds, or explicitly quantify their divergence. A convenient scenario pairing or historical correlation is not evidence of an identifiable causal intervention effect.

For a Strategic Value claim, the assessment must declare the focal beneficiary or authorized social-welfare aggregation before combining outcomes across actors. Benefits to counterparties, externalities, transfers and costs cannot be credited to the focal objective twice or silently converted between actors with incompatible utilities.

When a Strategic Value claim evaluates a sequential decision policy, the policy may condition each action only on observations and information available at the time of that action. A lookahead ranking must not exploit hindsight, future responses or post-action evidence as if they were known at decision time; posterior updates must preserve observation provenance.

For a Strategic Value claim about a portfolio or joint intervention, its value is evaluated against the joint feasible counterfactual and shared resource constraints. Standalone action values may be summed only with evidence of additive independence; shared dependencies, synergies, substitution, resource collision and cannibalization must be represented or remain unresolved.

When uncertainty can change preference in a Strategic Value comparison, the evaluation must expose a bounded sensitivity or uncertainty result and conditional decision boundary, not an unjustified precise winner. A robustness claim requires declared uncertainty sets, bounds or probability models and an applicable comparison method.

Claims of model-derived or independently verified Strategic Value require version-bound numerical method identity, input/assumption lineage, execution provenance and applicable, independently reviewable model-validation evidence appropriate to the claim. Empirical forecast validity may be supported by calibration, backtesting, sensitivity or out-of-sample evaluation where applicable, not presumed mathematical proof of general real-world adequacy. Arithmetic, projection receipts and model-validation evidence establish different things and cannot substitute for one another.
